body_text:
The Orbit-Stabilizer Theorem. Let a group $G$ act on a set $X$ via $\alpha$.
For any element $x \in X$, there is a natural bijection between the left coset
space $G / G_x$ and the orbit $G \cdot x$, given by:
$$ \Phi : G / G_x \longrightarrow G \cdot x, \quad \Phi(g G_x) = g \cdot x. $$
Consequently, if $G$ is finite:
$$ |G| = |G \cdot x| \cdot |G_x| = [G : G_x] \cdot |G_x|. $$

*Proof*:
- Well-Definedness and Injectivity: For $g, h \in G$:
  $$ g \cdot x = h \cdot x \iff h^{-1} \cdot (g \cdot x) = x \iff (h^{-1} * g) \cdot x = x \iff h^{-1} * g \in G_x \iff g G_x = h G_x. $$
  Reading left-to-right proves injectivity; reading right-to-left proves well-definedness.
- Surjectivity: By definition of the orbit, every $y \in G \cdot x$ is of the form
  $y = g \cdot x = \Phi(g G_x)$ for some $g \in G$.
Thus $\Phi$ is a well-defined bijection.
